introduction.text: Chiesa di Sant'Onofrio al Gianicolo is a historic Roman church on the Janiculum hill, notable as the titular church of the Order of the Holy Sepulchre and for its Renaissance architecture and rich artistic heritage.

history.description: St Onuphrius, a 4th‑century Egyptian hermit, is the patron saint of the church.
A hermitage founded by Nicola da Forca Palena around 1419 served as the basis for the later monastery.
The monastery was constructed around 1439 on the hermitage site.
Lunettes by Domenichino, painted in 1605, commemorate the hermits and depict scenes from St Jerome's life.
Since 1946 the church has been cared for by the American congregation of the Franciscan Friars of the Atonement.
The Salita di Sant'Onofrio was used as a location for the 1958 film Big Deal on Madonna Street.
Pierbattista Pizzaballa has served as the Cardinal‑Priest of the church since 2023.

design.description: The church features a Renaissance portico and a single cross‑vaulted nave with five chapels.
The cloister, possibly the oldest part of the complex, contains frescoes depicting scenes from St Onuphrius's life.
A fountain in the churchyard incorporates salvaged elements from the former Piazza Giudia fountain.

art.description: Lunettes by Domenichino (1605) celebrate hermits and illustrate scenes from St Jerome's life.
An altarpiece by Agostino Carracci, The Madonna of Loreto, is the artist's only work in a Roman church.
Frescoes in the apse by Baldassare Peruzzi depict scenes from the Life of Mary.
The first chapel to the right contains an Annunciation by Antoniazzo Romano and an Eternal Father attributed to Baldassarre Peruzzi.
The second chapel to the right features frescoes and stuccoes by Giovanni Battista Ricci (1605) and an altarpiece of the Madonna di Loreto by pupils of Annibale Carracci.
The third chapel on the left holds a monument to Torquato Tasso (1857) by Giuseppe De Fabris.
The second chapel on the left contains a Trinity fresco on the ceiling by Francesco Trevisani.
The sacristy ceiling is frescoed by Girolamo Pesci, while the walls feature a Peter of Pisa by Francesco Trevisani.
The cloister frescoes by Giuseppe Cesari (Cavaliere d'Arpino) and others depict scenes from the life of Saint Onuphrius.
